fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single access drive entrance clearly so responding units do not bypass it when approaching under low-visibility conditions.
• Clear dense vegetation along the sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Trim back vegetation where it crowds the exterior walls of the main residence and detached structures so responders can move around the buildings.
• Keep a cleared path along the walkway connecting structures so responders can move between buildings quickly.
• Create a flat, stable area near the end of the access drive that is large enough for an emergency vehicle to turn around and exit forward.
• Keep the access drive free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so a full-size emergency vehicle can travel its entire length.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structures to give responders clear sightlines and room to work around all sides.
• Post the physical address visibly at the main residence as a secondary marker in case the road entrance sign is missed.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Grass Cover; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Route; Limited Turnaround Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls and foundation.
• Remove dead or dry grass growing up against the base of the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree clusters near the house so individual trees are spaced apart and not touching each other or the structure.
• Raise the lowest branches on trees near the house by cutting limbs from the ground up to reduce how easily fire can climb into the tree canopy.
• Cut or mow the grass cover in the area immediately surrounding the house, especially during dry months.
• Clear brush from the area between the brush patch and the house so there is open, low-growth ground between them.
• Thin scattered trees around the property perimeter to break up continuous patches of vegetation leading toward the house.
• Keep the single access driveway clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and tall grass along both edges.
• Remove any brush or debris that has accumulated at the driveway entrance or along its length.
• Clear enough space at the end of the driveway or near the house for a vehicle to turn around without backing into vegetation.
• Move any woodpiles, propane tanks, or stored materials away from the house walls and out of dense vegetation.
